\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تحویل} \fa{گرفتن} (tahvil gereftan)}{تحویل گرفتن (tahvil gereftan)}]{\fa{تحویل} \fa{گرفتن} (tahvil gereftan) — to receive, to take delivery of; to check in (to a room)}

\label{lesson:FA-C438-tahvil-gereftan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a suite, then the Persian for to stay.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تحویل} \fa{گرفتن}}
\textbf{\fa{تحویل} \fa{گرفتن}} (\emph{tahvil gereftan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to receive, to take delivery of; to check in (to a room)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{ساعت} \fa{دو} \fa{اتاق} \fa{را} \fa{تحویل} \fa{گرفتیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Sâ'at-e do otâq râ tahvil gereftim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We got our room at two o'clock.
\end{quote}

The opposite of \emph{tahvil dâdan} 'to hand over'. Colloquially also to make a fuss of someone.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tahvil gereftan} is built from \emph{tahvil} 'handing over', a loan usually traced to Arabic \emph{taḥwīl} 'transfer, turning over' (EtymDB does not list it), and the native verb \emph{gereftan} 'to take', usually traced to Old Persian \emph{grab-}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tahvil gereftan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tahvil gereftan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{tahvil gereftan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a suite, then the Persian for to stay, then say \emph{tahvil gereftan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تسویه} \fa{حساب} \fa{کردن} (tasviye hesâb kardan)}{تسویه حساب کردن (tasviye hesâb kardan)}]{\fa{تسویه} \fa{حساب} \fa{کردن} (tasviye hesâb kardan) — to settle the bill, to settle up; to check out}

\label{lesson:FA-C438-tasviye-hesab-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to stay, then the Persian for to receive.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تسویه} \fa{حساب} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{تسویه} \fa{حساب} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{tasviye hesâb kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to settle the bill, to settle up; to check out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{صبح} \fa{با} \fa{هتل} \fa{تسویه} \fa{حساب} \fa{کردیم} \fa{و} \fa{رفتیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Sobh bâ hotel tasviye hesâb kardim va raftim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the morning we settled up with the hotel and left.
\end{quote}

\emph{tasviye} 'settling' + \emph{hesâb} 'account' + \emph{kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tasviye hesâb kardan} is built from \emph{tasviye} 'levelling, settling', a loan usually traced to Arabic \emph{taswiya}, \emph{hesâb} 'account', borrowed from Arabic \emph{ḥisāb} (EtymDB), and \emph{kardan} 'to do'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tasviye hesâb kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{tasviye hesâb kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to stay, then the Persian for to receive, then say \emph{tasviye hesâb kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{تسویه} \fa{حساب} \fa{کردن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To settle the bill, to settle up; to check out\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کارت} \fa{شناسایی} (kârt-e shenâsâyi)}{کارت شناسایی (kârt-e shenâsâyi)}]{\fa{کارت} \fa{شناسایی} (kârt-e shenâsâyi) — an identity card, an ID}

\label{lesson:FA-C438-kart-e-shenasayi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to receive, then the Persian for to settle the bill.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کارت} \fa{شناسایی}}
\textbf{\fa{کارت} \fa{شناسایی}} (\emph{kârt-e shenâsâyi}) — \textquotedblleft{}an identity card, an ID\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{پذیرش} \fa{کارت} \fa{شناسایی} \fa{مرا} \fa{خواستند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar paziresh kârt-e shenâsâyi-ye marâ khâstand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
At reception they asked for my ID card.
\end{quote}

\emph{shenâsâyi} 'identification', from \emph{shenâkhtan} 'to know, to recognize'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kârt-e shenâsâyi} is built from \emph{kârt} 'card', which EtymDB takes from French \emph{carte}, and native \emph{shenâsâyi} 'identification', from \emph{shenâs}, the present stem of \emph{shenâkhtan} 'to know, to recognize'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kârt-e shenâsâyi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{kârt-e shenâsâyi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to receive, then the Persian for to settle the bill, then say \emph{kârt-e shenâsâyi} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پیش} \fa{پرداخت} (pishpardâkht)}{پیش پرداخت (pishpardâkht)}]{\fa{پیش} \fa{پرداخت} (pishpardâkht) — a deposit, an advance payment}

\label{lesson:FA-C438-pishpardakht}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to settle the bill, then the Persian for an identity card.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پیش} \fa{پرداخت}}
\textbf{\fa{پیش} \fa{پرداخت}} (\emph{pishpardâkht}) — \textquotedblleft{}a deposit, an advance payment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{برای} \fa{رزرو} \fa{اتاق} \fa{پیش} \fa{پرداخت} \fa{دادیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Barâ-ye rezerv-e otâq pishpardâkht dâdim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We paid a deposit to book the room.
\end{quote}

\emph{pish} 'before' + \emph{pardâkht} 'payment'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pishpardâkht} is a native compound of \emph{pish} 'before', usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{pēš}, and \emph{pardâkht} 'payment', the past stem of \emph{pardâkhtan} 'to pay'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گاوصندوق} (gâvsanduq)}{گاوصندوق (gâvsanduq)}]{\fa{گاوصندوق} (gâvsanduq) — a safe, a strongbox}

\label{lesson:FA-C438-gavsanduq}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an identity card, then the Persian for a deposit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گاوصندوق}}
\textbf{\fa{گاوصندوق}} (\emph{gâvsanduq}) — \textquotedblleft{}a safe, a strongbox\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پولمان} \fa{را} \fa{در} \fa{گاوصندوق} \fa{هتل} \fa{گذاشتیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Pulemân râ dar gâvsanduq-e hotel gozâshtim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We put our money in the hotel safe.
\end{quote}

\emph{gâv} 'ox', here 'big and strong', + \emph{sanduq} 'chest'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gâvsanduq} is built from native \emph{gâv} 'ox', used for things that are big and heavy, and \emph{sanduq} 'chest, box', borrowed from Arabic \emph{ṣundūq} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
